#
# SIP torture test messages written for sipnab: provenance.
#
# These messages are original work, written for sipnab on 2026-11-25. None is
# a copy or an edit of an RFC message: no RFC message text was copied into
# them. Each one covers one torture case of RFC 4475 or RFC 5118, cited below
# by RFC and section number, and has the property that section tests.
#
# Values. Every name and address is reserved for documentation: example.com,
# example.net and example.org names (RFC 2606), the .test and .invalid
# top-level domains (RFC 6761), RFC 5737 IPv4 addresses (192.0.2.0/24,
# 198.51.100.0/24, 203.0.113.0/24), RFC 3849 IPv6 addresses (2001:db8::/32)
# and 555-0100 to 555-0199 telephone numbers. One address is not: the Via of
# rfc4475/3.3.10-bcast.dat is 255.255.255.255, the broadcast address that
# RFC 4475 section 3.3.10 tests. User names such as "desk" and "front" are
# roles, not people.
#
# Line ends are CRLF in every file, the RFC 5118 ones included.
#
# Two files keep a defect of the RFC's own message on purpose, so that each
# gets the verdict the RFC message gets (see the "note" lines):
# rfc4475/3.1.2.15-baddn.dat ends without the blank line after its headers,
# and rfc5118/4.6-ipv6-in-sdp.dat declares a Content-Length 17 octets larger
# than its body.
#
# Verdicts. tests/sip_torture_rfc_messages_test.rs runs each file through the
# parser, the linter and the dialog store. A local run on 2026-11-25 gave each
# file and the byte-exact message of its RFC section the same verdict, all 61
# of them; that test records those verdicts. The RFC messages are not in the
# repository.
#
# One entry per file: its path; "covers:" the RFC section; "tests:" the
# property it has; optional "note:" lines; "SHA-256:" the digest of the file,
# which the test checks.

rfc4475/3.1.1.1-wsinv.dat
  covers: RFC 4475 section 3.1.1.1
  tests: a valid INVITE with unusual whitespace and line folding, mixed-case and compact header names, escaped quotes in display names, leading zeros, unknown parameters and headers, an empty header and a top Via whose branch has no magic cookie
  SHA-256: 3d71ef481c5203fcfd2104a492a0e33d15529563752201b1f8f19c7e72f757ac

rfc4475/3.1.1.2-intmeth.dat
  covers: RFC 4475 section 3.1.1.2
  tests: every token character in the method, URI user and password, branch, tag and parameter names; quoted-pairs escaping BEL, NUL and DEL; UTF-8 in a quoted parameter and an extension header; Max-Forwards 200
  SHA-256: e15359e548cc1e36985209a7506eeab84d7b6c833a0fcff52e7aad27a172e6ab

rfc4475/3.1.1.3-esc01.dat
  covers: RFC 4475 section 3.1.1.3
  tests: % escapes of ':' and '@' in the Request-URI user part, of unreserved characters and a space in user parts, and in URI parameter names and values; Max-Forwards 99
  SHA-256: 9c5042583f7b2de302d87cbd885e8a72ab98084804f914355a95027bdd9c3c6c

rfc4475/3.1.1.4-escnull.dat
  covers: RFC 4475 section 3.1.1.4
  tests: escaped NUL octets (%00) in URI user parts
  SHA-256: 7a0c42317e578ab53c6e04af6e4cb7972948b0015a62d2f8035be326958ef179

rfc4475/3.1.1.5-esc02.dat
  covers: RFC 4475 section 3.1.1.5
  tests: '%' that is not an escape, in a method name, display names, a branch and a header name
  SHA-256: cd66f45dd47085f0dbfbc3d81b3f1094b6d13bc5d609ae6610a61ec25d114073

rfc4475/3.1.1.6-lwsdisp.dat
  covers: RFC 4475 section 3.1.1.6
  tests: no whitespace between a display name and '<'
  SHA-256: 06194bb08fbb442fa1cfff316afb27887753e5403c7d435110722e24f189330e

rfc4475/3.1.1.7-longreq.dat
  covers: RFC 4475 section 3.1.1.7
  tests: very long values in many header fields, 30 Via header fields in varied case and spacing, the top one with no branch
  SHA-256: 9c982e57ab04c8aacf703f647bf0e33913a1d1e1ad2918229dc869579d08d01e

rfc4475/3.1.1.8-dblreq.dat
  covers: RFC 4475 section 3.1.1.8
  tests: octets after the end of a REGISTER with Content-Length 0, in the same datagram
  SHA-256: f6e58b006375a42ebb6453b43dfb44dc8f8bcde6bca74745ca00dd66b128b114

rfc4475/3.1.1.9-semiuri.dat
  covers: RFC 4475 section 3.1.1.9
  tests: a ';' inside the Request-URI user part, and a folded Accept list
  SHA-256: c30d77da674a3887498d9cc073968c83a71bd3fab59bf2996dd2edc56104c6fa

rfc4475/3.1.1.10-transports.dat
  covers: RFC 4475 section 3.1.1.10
  tests: Via transports TCP, TLS, SCTP, UDP and one nobody knows
  SHA-256: 2271d93a9aacea3f87345bc79ef196b7207a99d95bc1c0906cf26172268057e7

rfc4475/3.1.1.11-mpart01.dat
  covers: RFC 4475 section 3.1.1.11
  tests: a multipart/mixed MESSAGE whose second part is 512 octets of raw binary
  SHA-256: 9a2d6c0b2799a1286313d7b0b36174e7a4a7366f838b070649e99e1d24b08bf1
